Record this pane (HERDR_PANE_ID) as your own seat, with operator/human provenance, so `thread create`, `invite`, `send`, `read`, `ack` and `accept` run here with no caller flags. Re-run after a daemon restart

Usage: herdr-threads me init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --operator
          Override the agent guard as the local account: record yourself over an agent's binding or where agent markers are present
      --state-dir <STATE_DIR>
          Select the local herdr-threads state directory. May repeat with an identical value; conflicting values are refused
      --host-endpoint <HOST_ENDPOINT>
          Select the local Herdr host socket path. May repeat with an identical value; conflicting values are refused
      --json
          Emit a structured JSON result on stdout
      --human
          Human-readable tables and transcripts (the default on a terminal)
      --machine
          The stable `key: value` text form for scripts and models (the default when stdout is not a terminal)
      --cooperative-seat <COOPERATIVE_SEAT>
          Explicit seat ID for a cooperative agent call; requires all four --cooperative-* options
      --cooperative-target <COOPERATIVE_TARGET>
          Exact live pane ID or scoped name bound to the cooperative seat
      --cooperative-harness <COOPERATIVE_HARNESS>
          Agent harness making the cooperative call [possible values: claude, codex, hermes, synthetic_fourth]
      --cooperative-role <COOPERATIVE_ROLE>
          Agent role for the cooperative call [possible values: top-level, subagent]
  -h, --help
          Print help

Run it in your own shell pane, then use `ht human` for thread create, invite, send, read, ack and accept there with no --cooperative-* flags. Your actions are recorded as operator_human, never as an agent. Messages remain readable, but a human seat owes no ACK and gets no overdue-ACK warning, even when a sender uses --require-ack. Re-run `human me init` after a daemon restart to mark yourself available again. It is refused where agent markers (CLAUDECODE, CODEX_SANDBOX, CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED) or a registered agent harness reported by Herdr are present, and over a seat bound to an agent; `human me init --operator` overrides that as the local account (later commands in this pane then run as you).
